newsitem.title: USA: Telesoft sees 1997 telemanagement sales up.
newsitem.headline: Telesoft sees 1997 telemanagement sales up.

text.p: Telesoft Corp said Wednesday it expects a new product from its telemanagement systems to boost fiscal 1997 sales in the division above historical levels.

"Our existing telemanagement system customer base has expressed strong interest for the new, and more powerful product, (called GUI, or graphical user interface)" the company said in a statement along with its third quarter earnings.
It said it expects its recently acquired Goodnet division to continue to operate at a loss through the end of 1996 and part of 1997.
It expects the Goodnet Division's subscriber base will show renewed growth in the first quarter of fiscal 1997, as the company integrates billing systems and resolves access delays.
"While gross revenues at the Goodnet Division are expected to continue to grow, we expect the division to continue to operate at a loss through the end of 1996, and part of 1997," the company said.
Earlier, Telesoft reported a loss of $0.13 a share on revenue of $3.2 million versus a profit of $0.02 a share on revenue of $2.7 million one year ago.

"Our third quarter is typically soft due to the seasonal fluctuation of the Student Telephone Services Division, which experiences low revenues during the summer vacation months," Telesoft Vice President of Finance Michael Zerbib said in a statement.

"The normal impact of this fluctuation on our results was exacerbated by reduced telemanagement system sales caused by delays in the release of our graphical user interface software package." System sales declined by $650,000 during the third quarter, causing the Telemanagement Division to have an operating loss for the period.
The Goodnet Division represented 9.1 percent, or $1,287,216 of total revenues and generated a pretax net loss of approximately $100,000, Zerbib said.
Telesoft designs and manages telecommunications systems to the higher education, corporate and governmental agency markets.
